subject.title: Feature request: fallback model chain for compaction and LCM summaryModel

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit fallback model-chain contract for embedded compaction now, and should the Lossless `summaryModel` fallback be plugin-owned or require a generic context-engine/plugin SDK seam first?
rationale: The issue is valid by source inspection, but the requested fix adds public config and crosses core compaction, provider/auth routing, and plugin-owned Lossless/context-engine behavior; automation should not choose that API contract.

options.title: Split embedded core and Lossless/plugin ownership
options.body: Accept an embedded-only `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` contract after maintainer review, and keep Lossless fallback support in the Lossless plugin or a generic SDK seam.

options.title: Design one unified summary fallback contract first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one cross-owner contract for embedded compaction, context engines, and Lossless summaries.

options.title: Decline new public config for now
options.body: Keep current session-fallback behavior for unset compaction models and point advanced users to provider/plugin-level alternatives instead of adding fallback arrays.

recommendation.title: Split embedded core and Lossless/plugin ownership
recommendation.body: Accept an embedded-only `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` contract after maintainer review, and keep Lossless fallback support in the Lossless plugin or a generic SDK seam.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this owner-boundary decision to compaction fallback behavior, compaction docs, and the compaction provider seam.
